title: emf-inversion-audit: code and data pipeline for "Rethinking the Reported Accuracy of Smartphone-Based Electric-Field Inversion for Crowdsourced EMF Monitoring"
description:
Code and data pipeline accompanying the paper Rethinking the Reported Accuracy of Smartphone-Based Electric-Field Inversion for Crowdsourced EMF Monitoring.

Starting from a public smartphone measurement campaign (Zeng et al., Radio Science, 2024), the repository reproduces a gradient-boosting electric-field inversion model and then varies three factors that are usually fixed by convention:

  • Evaluation protocol — random hold-out, spatio-temporal patch-based cross-validation with an embargo, and leave-one-(campaign, band)-out. Protocol choice moves the error estimate by 0.39 dB, more than twice the spread among six regressors.
  • Band information — adding the reported EARFCN removes a band-dependent bias of up to 0.5 dB and lowers MAE by 15–31 % depending on how the label is defined.
  • Device calibration — input-space recalibration of the same handset is absorbed by the tree ensemble; only cross-device offsets matter, and 100 labelled samples recover 65–75 % of the loss.

The dataset is not redistributed here; it is available from figshare (DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.25034537.v1).
